    {"start": "00:20", "end": "00:24", "speech": "Because then it just flashes on the screen and the user's brain registers like 'something weird just happened'."},
    {"start": "00:24", "end": "00:27", "speech": "You actually make it feel slower, so if it's under 1 second, just show the results."},
    {"start": "00:27", "end": "00:30", "speech": "Okay, so what if your action takes longer than a second?"},
    {"start": "00:30", "end": "00:33", "speech": "A plain spinner with no text works for about 2 to 5 seconds."},
    {"start": "00:33", "end": "00:36", "speech": "And past 5 seconds, a spinner with no text starts to feel broken."},
    {"start": "00:36", "end": "00:39", "speech": "The user has no idea what's happening and the patience starts to drop very quickly."},
    {"start": "00:39", "end": "00:45", "speech": "So you have some static text: 'Loading...' or 'Saving...', and that buys you maybe one more second."},

    {"start": "00:51", "end": "00:54", "speech": "This is where people are willing to wait significantly longer."},
    {"start": "00:54", "end": "00:57", "speech": "Because they feel that there's action happening, even if it's fake."},
    {"start": "00:57", "end": "01:00", "speech": "But all of this works up to about 10 seconds."},
    {"start": "01:00", "end": "01:03", "speech": "After 10 seconds, looped animations just stop working."},

    {"start": "01:10", "end": "01:15", "speech": "Past 10 seconds, you need a different approach: a progress bar, a step-by-step indicator, something else."},
